choices.text: The drawing is fine - atoms are solid balls
Atoms are mostly empty space, with electrons in shells around a tiny dense nucleus
Atoms are solid, but the nucleus is hollow
The electrons fill the whole ball evenly

questions.feedback: If you picked the solid ball, that is the trap: Atoms are solid balls. Reteach point: Atoms are mostly empty space: the electrons sit far from a tiny dense nucleus. Use the shell model, not the planet model.
questions.prompt: A student draws an atom as a solid ball. What is the best correction?

questions.answer: Almost all the mass is concentrated in the tiny dense nucleus, because it holds the protons and neutrons while electrons have almost no mass.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names the nucleus and the protons and neutrons inside it. An answer that spreads the mass over the whole atom is still picturing a solid ball.
questions.prompt: In one sentence, say where the mass of an atom is concentrated and why.

questions.feedback: Neutrons = nucleon number - proton number = 24 - 12 = 12. If you answered 24, you used the nucleon number alone; if 36, you added instead of subtracting.
questions.prompt: Magnesium has proton number 12 and nucleon number 24. How many neutrons does it have?

questions.answer: Period 3, because it has three electron shells; group 5, because it has 5 electrons in its outer shell.
questions.feedback: Period counts the shells, group counts the outer electrons. Swapping the two numbers is the common slip - check which count you used for each.
questions.prompt: An element has electron arrangement 2,8,5. State its period and its group, and explain each answer.
